title: NiWo: An Augmentation Framework to Enhance ML Performance and Interpretability for Tabular Data with Class Imbalance

problem.claim: Class imbalance is a challenge in machine learning and artificial intelligence tasks across multiple data modalities.

gap.claim: For real-world tabular datasets with thousands of instances, integrating explanation tools into augmentation is computationally expensive.

narrative_sequence.summary: Data augmentation methods have been proposed to address class imbalance across data modalities.
Tabular-data augmentation should be interpretable so human decision-makers can audit which neighborhoods are augmented and why.
This interpretability requirement is especially important in high-stakes domains.
Previous studies used explanation tools to derive instance-level weights that guide augmentation while preserving interpretability.
The complexity of explanation tools makes this integration computationally expensive on real-world datasets with thousands of instances.

source_observation.claim: Interpretability is required for auditing tabular-data augmentation, while explanation-based integration can be computationally expensive at scale.

interpretation.claim: Augmentation design may need to balance auditability against explanation cost.

application.claim: When evaluating augmentation for high-stakes tabular data, assess both the auditability of augmentation decisions and the computational cost of producing explanations.

exception.claim: The supplied units do not establish that this tradeoff applies beyond tabular data or datasets with thousands of instances.

unknowns: The proposed NiWo framework and its mechanism are not described.
No empirical results, datasets, baselines, metrics, or comparisons are supplied.
No explicit novelty claim is supplied.
